problem: Existing VLN agents show a consistent gap between Success Rate and Oracle Success Rate (up to ~9% on R2R, 3-4% on REVERIE): the agent passes the target viewpoint but fails to stop there. Prior work only improves per-step action prediction and ignores this gap.
motivation: A high OSR means the correct location is already visited in the trajectory, so a large SR gain is available by picking the right stop point post hoc. The task resembles temporal video grounding (localize the target frame given text), but trajectories are sparse panoramas with abrupt cutaways and few matching images.
key_idea: Treat the SR-OSR gap as a trajectory grounding problem: an add-on transformer takes a trajectory from any off-the-shelf VLN model plus the instruction, and picks the viewpoint most likely to be the destination.
insight: The gain comes from re-scoring visited viewpoints, not from better actions: OSR stays unchanged while SR rises, and the gap on R2R val-unseen (HOP) shrinks from 7.96 to 4.56. Ablations show all three modules matter (removing the elevation transformer hurts most: SR 65.79 vs 66.92). Training on constructed trajectories (target not always last) plus HM3D data helps (HM3D alone gives only 45.52 SR). Focal+Dice beats BCE (66.92 vs 63.62).
method: Trajectory harvesting: run a pretrained VLN model (HOP, HAMT, DUET, SIG variants) to get a trajectory of T panoramic viewpoints (36 views each: 3 elevations x 12 headings).
Text/vision encoders: BERT/RoBERTa [CLS] token as instruction feature; frozen ViT-B/16 image features plus step and spatial sinusoidal encodings.
Cross-Modality Elevation Transformer: fuses each view feature with the instruction via FC, then applies self-attention across the 3 elevations per heading and average-pools, reducing tokens to 1/3.
Spatial-Temporal Transformer: attention across 12 headings within each viewpoint, then across all T x 12 tokens for long-range trajectory dependency.

Target Selection Transformer: learnable per-viewpoint queries self-attend and cross-attend to compress each viewpoint to one vector; a 2-layer MLP + sigmoid gives target probability; the argmax viewpoint is chosen at inference.

Training data construction: sample 1-2 positive viewpoints within 3 m of the goal, build new paths via shortest path from the start plus a sub-path of up to 6 m beyond, so the target is not always last (396,866 trajectories on R2R, 331,533 on REVERIE, 376,871 on NDH, 427,347 on RxR).
Loss: Focal Loss (alpha=0.25, gamma=2) + Dice Loss with weights 1 and 0.1, trained with AdamW for 40k iterations.

setting.backbone: Frozen ViT-B/16 + RoBERTa/BERT text encoder (LR 1e-5), 2+2+2-layer transformer modules trained from scratch, applied on top of frozen baseline VLN agents' trajectories
setting.training_data: Constructed trajectories from R2R/REVERIE/NDH/RxR ground-truth paths (about 330k-430k each) plus HM3D-AutoVLN data (900 HM3D environments)
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB (36 views: 3 elevations x 12 headings) along a pre-computed trajectory, plus the instruction
setting.action_space: Discrete nav-graph viewpoints; post-hoc selection of the stop viewpoint among visited nodes (return path or cropped path)
setting.privileged: none (uses trajectories from a baseline VLN model; the destination may be absent from them)

numbers.extra: Trained with HM3D-AutoVLN extra data; return-path setting

numbers_note: Table values are printed as integers for R2R. The R2R crop-setting REVERIE table has apparent typos (e.g. SPL 54.63 with SR 32.83 for HOP crop). The RxR benchmark appears only in the appendix. NDH is mapped to CVDN.
results: Applied on top of four strong VLN agents, the method raises R2R val-unseen SR by 2-4 points (SIG_DUET 72→76, DUET 72→75, HOP 64→67) and test SR to 74. Gains on REVERIE are 0.35-2.33 SR, on NDH 1.9-2.7 SR, and on RxR 3.2 SR (HAMT). OSR is unchanged since it only re-selects among visited nodes.
limitations: Cannot recover when the target is absent from the given trajectory, so SR is bounded by OSR.
Post-hoc correction requires a return path (lowering SPL by ~1%) or a cropped-path SPL that is not a true executed path; it also cannot change object grounding (RGS).
Requires a separate model trained on synthetic trajectories and extra HM3D data, adding inference and training cost.
